biggestGap: Invert the chrome contrast. Every seam and bar edge on this screen is DARKER than its panel; in reference/shots/ui-bar.png every one is BRIGHTER. Measured: our horizontal and vertical dividers are #0A0F14 (luma 14.3) on a #13171B panel (luma 22.4); the reference's divider at y=948 is #2E332F (luma 49.6) on a panel of luma ~20 — 2.5x the panel, not 0.6x. Our empty-track outline is #1D2124 (1.45x panel); the reference's is #393C3D / #313435 (2.6x panel). And our gold fill ends in one antialiased pixel (168 -> 124 -> 22.4 track) where the reference's fill cap peaks at #FFF1B4 (luma 239, brighter than its own 186 body) and bleeds a 35px warm bloom into the track (114, 89, 75, 67, 57, 53, 48 ... 24). Fix all three together: raise --c-track's stroke to ~2.5x panel luma, replace --c-groove with a light hairline of the same value, and give every bar a hot cap plus a trailing glow. Then delete the 'dividers are DARKER than their panel' HARD RULE from tokens.css — it is transcribed from ui-bar.md, the PNG contradicts it, and the PNG wins. Until this lands the panels read as one flat slab and the bars read as painted rectangles instead of lit metal, which is the entire reason the blind A/B is not close.
evidence: CRITIC PASS. Judged from pixels, not source: ran `node tools/serve.mjs`, opened http://localhost:5174/skills.html at 390x844 (DPR 2, 780x1688 PNGs) and let it run untouched. Captured t=0, 6.5s, 7.5s, 8.5s, 9.5s, 20s, 62s, plus ?view=list and ?demo=levelup at 2.2/3.2/4.2s. All colour claims below are programmatic pixel samples from the PNGs, not eyeballing.

IT IS ALIVE, AND THE LOOP IS CAUSAL. 62s unattended: 27 actions, 890 XP, timer 00:01:02, skill 46 -> 47, mastery 34 -> 35 -> 36, stored ingots 212 -> 241, Coalstone 806 -> 756. Crossing the 50% pool checkpoint visibly rewrote the interval line from '2.40s of 3.00s - 20%' to '2.20s of 3.00s - 20% -0.2s' and moved the HELD/NEXT rows from 25%/50% to 50%/95%. A checkpoint changing the action interval in front of you is the hardest thing on the brief and it is done.

THE DISPLAY IS BOUND TO THAT MATH, NOT FAKED. Screen at t=62 reads '774 / 7,887 XP' for 47->48; deltaXp(48) computes to exactly 7887. 'TOTAL XP 75.9K' = xpAt(47) 75,127 + 774 = 75,901. Checkpoints follow the Melvor pattern without copying content (50% = an interval cut, mirroring Mining's -0.2s; 95% = mastery XP everywhere, mirroring Firemaking) on a 4.50M base cap = 500,000 x 9 recipes, which is the published rule.

DIVIDER POLARITY IS INVERTED vs the adjudicating PNG. Column scan x=100: our panel 22.4 luma, divider rows y=558-559 at #0A0F14 = 14.3. Vertical rule at x=272-273 identical. Reference column x=500: panel 19-22 luma, divider y=948-949 at #2E332F/#272B2D = 49.6/42.3. tokens.css encodes the wrong polarity as trap 2 of a 'HARD RULE' block, so this error is now load-bearing for every future piece.

OUR GOLD IS MATTE WHERE THE REFERENCE'S IS LIT. Bar heights match (ours 18px@2x = 9 CSS, ref 26px@2.585x = 10 CSS) and our top highlight is fine (222.6 vs 229.3), but our fill bottoms out at #BA8E3C luma 145 against the reference's #D5A440 luma 167, and we have no leading-cap hot spot and no bloom at all. Row scan across our cap: 168, 168, 124, then 22.4. The reference: 239, 227, 114, 89, 75, 67, 57, 53, 48, 46, 42, 38 ... 24 over ~35px.

TWO THUMB-TEST FAILURES AGAINST THE PROJECT'S OWN TOKEN. tokens.css declares --tap-min: 44px. Measured in-page: .runbtn (the play/pause — the single most important control on an idle screen) is 38x38, and .backbtn is 87x30. Everything else passes: .rrow recipe rows 356x79, .nav__item 72x47, and document scrollWidth == innerWidth == 390 so there is no horizontal scroll.

THE 12/16/20 RHYTHM IS DECLARED BUT NOT OBEYED. tokens.css ships --s-1..--s-8 as 4/8/12/16/20/24/32/40 and says 'nothing is off-grid'. Computed styles inside #viewRoot use gap 7px (.skillhead__eyebrow), gap 6px (.skillhead__status), gap/margin 5px and 6px (.lvlrow), and margin 10px (.divider). The optical letter-spacing compensations (2.34px, 3.74px) are legitimate; the 5/6/7px gaps are not.

THE PLAQUES CLIP LIVE TEXT WITH NO SCRIM. On the level-up shot the gold plaque sits over the pool panel and cuts the HELD and NEXT rows mid-row, leaving the words 'HELD' and 'NEXT' truncated at its left edge and '95%' reduced to '%' at its right, while the violet checkpoint bullets for those same rows still poke out beside it. The mastery plaque does the same. It reads as a card dropped on a live panel rather than a moment the panel makes room for.

NO GOLD METAL EXISTS ANYWHERE ON THIS SCREEN. The reference's signature component is the CLAIM plate: chamfered, gold-gradient-filled, inner bevel, the one high-saturation object in its panel. Our screen has zero filled-gold surfaces. The play/pause is a flat dark rounded square with a grey glyph, and the level-up plaque — the emotional peak of the whole loop — is a dark box with a 1px gold outline. Chamfers and gold hairlines are present; pressed metal is not.

ICONS ARE FLAT GLYPHS AGAINST RENDERED OBJECTS. The five discipline marks, the pause glyph and the checkpoint diamonds are single-colour SVG wireframes. The reference's coin, gem, energy orb, sword, shield and crown are all beveled, specular, 3D-ish renders. Our coin and shard chips are the closest and still read a tier below. In the list view this is the loudest 'not shipped' tell.

THE POOL BAR READS AS BROKEN, NOT SEGMENTED. Checkpoint ticks are cut through the violet fill as hard dark notches, so at 56.2% the Emberdelving row in the list looks like four disconnected violet blocks rather than one bar. The reference's 92% UPGRADE bar is one continuous lozenge. This is the 'depth without noise' rule going the wrong way.

THE POOL NUMBER NEVER MOVES, SO THE CHECKPOINT HAS NO NUMERIC WITNESS. '2.25M / 4.50M' is identical at t=0 and t=62 even though the 50% pip flipped from hollow to filled and the interval changed. There is no pool percentage figure anywhere, so the one number that would prove the crossing is absent from a screen whose entire job is making the loop legible.

WHAT IS ALREADY GOOD AND SHOULD NOT BE TOUCHED: the two-axis colour discipline (gold = level/XP/interval/yield, violet = mastery/pool/checkpoints) holds without a single leak across both views; labels sit at --c-text-2 and are genuinely light rather than dimmed, with hierarchy carried by size and letter-spacing exactly as the reference does it; figures are tabular throughout; the whole loop fits above the fold at 390x844 with the pool panel bottom at y=779 against a 784 fold; percentages floor rather than round; and `npm run verify` passes 20/20 including no-raw-hex.

BLIND A/B: I stripped labels and asked which is the shipped commercial product. The reference, and not narrowly. Composition, type and information design are close enough that ours does not embarrass itself — but every surface in ours is matte and every seam is invisible, so it reads as a very accomplished design-system implementation OF the reference rather than the reference. The systems half of this piece is arguably shippable today; the chrome half is a high-fidelity mockup.
